# Chapter 7: Exceptions — 7.3–7.5

Rules that no analyzer enforces (judgment), CONSIDER rules that analyzers only suggest, and rules that analyzers check only in part, marked "(partly checked)". Open the examples file for the explanation and code the book gives with each rule.

## 7.3.1 Exception and SystemException

- **FDG7038** DO NOT catch `System.Exception` or `System.SystemException` in framework code, unless you intend to rethrow. (partly checked) (library only)
- **FDG7039** AVOID catching `System.Exception` or `System.SystemException`, except in top-level exception handlers. (partly checked)

## 7.3.3 InvalidOperationException

- **FDG7041** DO throw an `InvalidOperationException` if the object is in an inappropriate state. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7041

## 7.3.4 ArgumentException, ArgumentNullException, and ArgumentOutOfRangeException

- **FDG7042** DO throw `ArgumentException` or one of its subtypes if bad arguments are passed to a member. Prefer the most derived exception type, if applicable.
- **FDG7043** DO set the `ParamName` property when throwing one of the subclasses of `ArgumentExceptions`. (partly checked) — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7043
- **FDG7044** DO use `value` for the name of the implicit value parameter of property setters. (partly checked) — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7044

## 7.3.5 NullReferenceException, IndexOutOfRangeException, and AccessViolationException

- **FDG7045** DO NOT allow publicly callable APIs to explicitly or implicitly throw `NullReferenceException`, `AccessViolationException`, or `IndexOutOfRangeException`. These exceptions are reserved and thrown by the platform and in most cases indicate a bug. (partly checked) (library only) — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7045

## 7.3.6 StackOverflowException

- **FDG7047** DO NOT catch `StackOverflowException`. (partly checked) — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7047

## 7.3.9 OperationCanceledException and TaskCanceledException

- **FDG7050** DO throw `OperationCanceledException` to represent any caller-initiated abort or cancellation.
- **FDG7051** DO prefer catching `OperationCanceledException` to `TaskCanceledException`. (partly checked) — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7051

## 7.3.10 FormatException

- **FDG7052** DO throw `FormatException` to indicate the input string in a text parsing method does not conform to the required, or specified, format.
- **FDG7053** DO throw `FormatException` to indicate the format specifier string to a text parsing or text formatting method is invalid. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7053

## 7.3.11 PlatformNotSupportedException

- **FDG7054** DO throw `PlatformNotSupportedException` to indicate the operation cannot complete in the current runtime environment but could on a different runtime or operating system. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7054

## 7.4 Designing Custom Exceptions

- **FDG7055** DO derive exceptions from `System.Exception` or one of the other common base exceptions.
- **FDG7056** AVOID deep exception hierarchies. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7056
- **FDG7058** DO make exceptions runtime serializable. An exception must be serializable to work correctly across application domain and remoting boundaries. (partly checked)
- **FDG7059** DO provide (at least) these common constructors on all exceptions. Make sure the names and types of the parameters are exactly as shown in the following example. (partly checked) — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7059
- **FDG7060** CONSIDER providing exception properties for programmatic access to extra information (besides the message string) relevant to the exception.

## 7.5 Exceptions and Performance

- **FDG7061** DO NOT use error codes because of concerns that exceptions might affect performance negatively. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7061

## 7.5.1 The Tester–Doer Pattern

- **FDG7062** CONSIDER the Tester–Doer Pattern for members that might throw exceptions in common scenarios to avoid performance problems related to exceptions. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7062

## 7.5.2 The Try Pattern

- **FDG7063** CONSIDER the Try Pattern for members that might throw exceptions in common scenarios to avoid performance problems related to exceptions. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7063
- **FDG7064** DO use the prefix “Try” and Boolean return type for methods implementing the Try pattern. (partly checked)
- **FDG7065** DO pick one kind of reason for why your Try method can return `false`, and throw an exception for any other failure reason. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7065
- **FDG7066** DO provide an exception-throwing member for each member using the Try Pattern. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7066

## 7.5.2.1 Value-Producing Try Methods

- **FDG7067** DO “return” the value from a Try method via an `out` parameter. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7067
- **FDG7068** DO write `default(T)` to the `out` parameter from a Try method that returns `false`. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7068
- **FDG7069** AVOID writing to the `out` parameter from a Try method when throwing an exception. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7069

## 7.5.2.1 Static TryParse(string, out T) Methods

- **FDG7070** DO return `false` on null inputs to a method of the form `static bool TryParse(string, out T value)`. — examples: examples/ch07-exceptions-7-3-on.md#fdg7070
